subject: Customer query: SIG/SOC2 log deletion SLA for R&D sandboxes
messages:
From: Alex Greene <security@neurovantage.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-12T08:14:00Z
Subject: SIG + SOC2 question: sandbox log deletion timing

Hi Marcus,

Quick one — as part of our vendor SIG/SOC2 review the auditor flagged a question about how Redwood handles deletion of inference logs from non-production tenants (R&D/sandbox environments). Their request: can you confirm whether logs from sandbox tenants can be configured to be purged within 30 days and, if so, provide sample evidence (export of a sample log record and suggested language for SIG responses)?

We attached our SIG spreadsheet with the specific questions noted (see attachment). For context: NeuroVantage has a policy that non-prod test data must be deletable within 30 days, and our compliance team wants explicit confirmation and artifacts to close the ticket.

Appreciate a quick confirmation or proposed path forward — auditor timeline is tight (they want something by EOD Monday local).

Thanks,
Alex Greene
Security Manager | NeuroVantage
Attachments: neurovantage_SIG_questions.xlsx
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Greene <security@neurovantage.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-12T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG + SOC2 question: sandbox log deletion timing

Alex — thanks for the note and the spreadsheet. Looping in Karthik (infra/serving runtime) and Neha (compliance) so we can give a complete answer.

High level: we treat "sandbox" or non-production tenants differently from production tenants in two ways: 1) customers can opt-in to an accelerated TTL for telemetry/debug logs (down to 30 days) and 2) we can provide an export of raw log records prior to deletion for customer archival. Production telemetry tied to SOC2 scope typically defaults to the audit retention period your org requests, but sandboxes are configurable.

I've attached a short SLA matrix that shows the supported retention windows and evidence we can provide. Can you confirm the SIG row(s) you need answered (we saw a few items flagged in your spreadsheet)? Also, if the auditor needs an exported sample CSV, please indicate schema preference — we can produce a 10-row sample by EOD Monday.

Proposed next steps:
- We confirm whether you want: (A) accelerated deletion to 30 days for sandbox tenant(s), or (B) continue with standard retention but provide export/archive on request.
- If you choose A, we will provide: policy statement for SIG, sample export (CSV), and a screenshot of the TTL configuration in the Console.

We attached the SLA matrix (redwood_sla_matrix.pdf) for quick reference.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_sla_matrix.pdf
From: Alex Greene <security@neurovantage.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: NeuroVantage Legal <legal@neurovantage.com>
Date: 2029-05-12T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG + SOC2 question: sandbox log deletion timing

Thanks Marcus — NeuroVantage prefers option A (accelerated deletion to 30 days) for all sandboxes.

Auditor also asked for a sample export showing the available fields (timestamp, request_id, model, prompt_hash, response_length, tenant_id, redact_flags) so they can validate the scope of what will be deleted. I attached a small sample from our side to show the fields they expect — can you map that to your export and provide a 10-row sample?

If you can also provide the exact SIG language to put in their workbook, that would help close the item quickly.

Appreciate it — 
Alex
Attachments: sandbox_log_sample.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-12T13:00:00Z
Subject: Internal: NeuroVantage wants 30d TTL for sandboxes + SIG wording / sample export

Karthik / Neha —

NeuroVantage (external) is asking to set their sandbox tenants to 30d retention and needs: (1) SIG-friendly language we can paste into their spreadsheet, (2) a 10-row CSV sample matching the fields they listed, and (3) screenshots/evidence of the TTL config in Console. Auditor wants these by EOD Monday (their local).

Questions:
- Karthik: operationally, can we flip sandbox tenants to 30d TTL immediately and produce a sample export scoped to the tenant_id? Any caveats re: KV cache traces or derivative logs we should call out?
- Neha: compliance review — is there any SOC2 control language we should avoid promising (e.g., retention guarantees for production logs)? Also, confirm the suggested SIG wording (I want to send clean copy to Alex).

I'll hold on external confirmation until I get your replies.

Thanks,
Marcus
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: 2029-05-13T16:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Internal: NeuroVantage wants 30d TTL for sandboxes + SIG wording / sample export

Marcus —

Short answers: yes on the 30d TTL for sandbox tenants; we have a per-tenant TTL flag for telemetry/debug logs that can be set immediately (no downtime). Export: we can run a tenant-scoped export that includes the fields Alex listed. Caveats:
- We do not delete derived artifacts that customers have explicitly exported to their own storage (S3/Drive).
- KV cache entries used for persistent session acceleration are short-lived and not part of audit telemetry; if the auditor needs them explicitly called out, we should state they are ephemeral and not retained beyond the configured TTL.

Suggested SIG language (copy/paste):
"Redwood Inference supports per-tenant configurable telemetry retention windows. For non-production (sandbox) tenants, customers may request an accelerated time-to-delete as low as 30 days. Redwood can provide tenant-scoped exports of raw telemetry prior to deletion and will supply configuration screenshots and export artifacts as evidence. Production telemetry retention remains subject to customer contract and SOC2-scoped agreements."

Evidence we can provide by 2029-05-13 EOD US:
- 10-row CSV export (tenant-scoped) — will redact PII per our data handling policy; schema: timestamp, request_id, model, prompt_hash, response_length, tenant_id, redact_flags.
- Console screenshot showing TTL setting for the tenant.
- Short policy snippet on how sandbox TTLs are applied and how exported artifacts are handled.

I'll trigger the export now and place artifacts in the shared drive folder (will share link when ready).

Karthik
Infra Lead | Redwood Inference
